algorithm_long: RudraNet is a novel hybrid recursive architecture (Hybrid-Attention-MLP-Recursive-Model) designed specifically for low-data materials property prediction. It features an Attention-based Feature Extractor (AFE) that utilizes multi-head self-attention on tokenized elemental and stoichiometric descriptors, followed by a cross-attention gating mechanism with Mat2Vec embeddings. The core reasoning engine is a recursive MLP-TRM loop with shared weights that performs iterative state refinement over 20 discrete steps. The model is trained using a linear-weighted Deep Supervision loss and Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) to ensure generalizability on small tabular datasets.
notes: RudraNet corresponds to TRIADS Hybrid V13A for matbench_steels. Training was performed on Kaggle using one NVIDIA T4 GPU; the reported total elapsed training time was under 20 minutes, with exact timing unavailable. Due to access restrictions encountered in the Kaggle environment, the training script loaded the dataset via matminer and reproduced five shuffled KFold partitions with random_state=18012019, plus an inner training/validation holdout. Official fold index equivalence and the historical model-selection protocol remain to be independently verified. The code downloads pretrained Mat2Vec embeddings from https://storage.googleapis.com/mat2vec/. See https://github.com/Rtx09x/TRIADS for the research archive. Results and methodology remain subject to upstream review.
